purpose: silver_ourairports_runways is the cleaned, one-row-per-runway view of bronze.ourairports_runways (10760 rows), carrying runway identity, the parent airport reference, physical dimensions and surface, lighted and closed indicators, and the low-end and high-end threshold geometry. It feeds airport and runway analytics downstream and is the join partner for airport-level silver tables via airport_ref or airport_ident.
usage: Read one row per runway, keyed by id (distinct_count 10760 equals row_count 10760). Join to airport tables on airport_ref or airport_ident, both of which repeat across the 7591 distinct airports in this table. Use is_closed deliberately: closed runways are retained, so filter them out for operational analysis. Coordinate, elevation and heading columns are null for roughly 22 to 28 percent of rows and the displaced threshold columns for roughly 88 to 90 percent, so always guard aggregations against nulls rather than assuming full coverage.
limitations: Cleanup is structural only: no value was imputed and no row was removed, since duplicate_row_rate is 0.0. The surface vocabulary is unnormalised (239 distinct values with variants like "ASP", "ASPH" and "ASPH-CONC"), and le_ident and he_ident contain non-designator entries such as "." and "-12" that were left as-is. Range anomalies survive the cleanup: length_ft and width_ft have minima of 0.0 and 1.0 respectively and he_heading_degt has a max of 362.0 beyond the 360-degree compass range. The casts of id and airport_ref from VARCHAR to INTEGER rest on the 10 sampled values per column allowed by the profiler cap and should be verified against the full column before approval.
